street.description: Hyper-casual, street-level Cairene/Delta speech. Short sentences, slang-heavy, profanity-adjacent. Used in TikTok comedy, micro-influencer DMs, friends chatting. Not appropriate for brand-owned channels unless brand is explicitly edgy/youth.

casual_social.description: The default register for almost all Egyptian B2C social media. Natural, warm, conversational — how a 25-year-old native posts on their personal Instagram. Light English code-switching is expected and natural.

professional_casual.description: Polished but still recognizably Egyptian. Slang dialed down to 1-2 anchor terms; English loanwords kept for tech/marketing terms only. The voice of LinkedIn Egypt, B2B blog posts, white papers with personality.
avoid_when: luxury brands wanting heritage feel — go corporate_formal/MSA

corporate_formal.description: MSA-leaning Egyptian — almost entirely Modern Standard Arabic but with Egyptian rhythm and sentence structure. The voice of bank communications, government PSAs, luxury heritage brands, regulated industries.
avoid_when: any consumer social media — feels stiff and dated

egyptian_idioms: اللي اختشوا ماتوا (the shameless ones outlived the rest — sarcasm)
ابن الكلب (lit. son of a dog — very strong, almost never in marketing)
ع راسي (my pleasure / on my head)
تسلم ايديك (your hands deserve health — praise for craftsmanship/cooking)
ربنا يخليك (may God preserve you — gratitude/farewell)
حلال عليك (you've earned it / good for you)
ع راحتك (take your time / your call)
خليها على الله (leave it to God / stop stressing)

grammar_quirks: Negation with ما...ش circumfix: مفيش (there isn't), معرفش (I don't know), مبيعرفش (he doesn't know), ماحدش (no one), مفهمتش (I didn't understand)
Future tense particle ها prefixed to verbs: هاروح (I'll go), هايجي (he'll come), هتعمل (you'll do)
Present continuous بـ prefix: بيشتغل (he's working), بتاكل (you're eating), بيدور (he's looking)
Question words: إيه (what), إزاي (how), فين (where), إمتى (when), ليه (why), مين (who), كام (how much/many)
Possessive marker بتاع/بتاعت/بتوع: العربية بتاعتي (my car), البيت بتاعنا (our house) — distinct from MSA إضافة
Demonstratives ده/دي/دول come AFTER the noun: المنتج ده (this product), البنت دي (this girl), الناس دول (these people)
Pluralization of imperative with و: روحوا (you-pl. go), اعملوا (you-pl. do), شوفوا (you-pl. see)
Cairo qaf ق → glottal stop ء (e.g. قلب → ألب, قال → ال) — but NOT in Saidi/Upper Egypt where ق → g
Jeem ج → hard g in Cairo (gameel for جميل) — opposite of MSA's soft j
Vowel reduction: short i and u often dropped (e.g. كتاب → ktab, فهمت → fhimt)
Object pronoun suffixes attach to verbs: شفته (I saw him), حبيتها (I loved her), قالهم (he told them)

code_switching_patterns.english_in_arabic: Heavy in Cairo/Alex urban tech, marketing, and Gen Z scenes. Common pattern: Arabic syntax with English content nouns and adjectives. Examples: 'يعني الـ vibe مش حلو خالص', 'اعمل ستوري عن الـ event', 'البوست ده trending جامد', 'البراند بتاعهم professional أوي'. Verbs almost always stay Arabic; English verbs only appear in tech jargon ('بيـ debug الكود').
code_switching_patterns.french_in_arabic: Older generation (60+), historically Heliopolis/Zamalek/Garden City demographics. Phrases like 'مرسي يا حبيبتي', 'بون جور', 'شيك أوي'. In modern marketing, French loanwords surface in luxury, fashion, and beauty verticals — never in mass-market or Gen Z copy.
rules: English words are inserted as nouns/adjectives, never as full clauses. 'I'm going to the store' would never code-switch to '*أنا going للـ store' — that's broken. Natural: 'أنا رايح الـ store'.
Stress and pronunciation stay Arabic — English words get Arabic phonology (e.g. 'فايب' not 'vaib').
Avoid forced code-switching in luxury, heritage, religious, or government brands — they signal authenticity through cleaner Arabic.
When the audience age is mixed or skews older (gen_x/boomer), reduce English to ~5% of words.
Gen Z TikTok scripts can hit 30-40% English insertion and still feel native — but only if the rhythm holds.

do_not_use: تحفة as a primary excitement word — overused by every brand since ~2012, signals lazy copywriting. Use sparingly and only with self-aware framing.
روش / روشة — felt fresh in 2008-2014, now reads as dated millennial. Acceptable only when targeting 35+ audience nostalgically.
Khaleeji-specific vocabulary in Egyptian content: يبه, ابغى, شلونك, زين, وش — these are wrong-dialect markers and immediately tank credibility.
Levantine markers: كيفك, شو, هلق, منيح, كتير — wrong dialect.
MSA in casual social copy: هذا, ذلك, الذي, التي, إن, لكن, كذلك — sounds like a news anchor and kills engagement.
Religious phrases as ironic punchlines or comedic devices in commercial work — culturally damaging.
Saidi accent rendered phonetically for jokes (gameel for جميل played for laughs) — punching down, avoid absent legitimate cultural-partnership context.
Forced direct translation of English Gen Z slang ('on fleek' → 'على الفليك', 'low-key' → 'لو-كي') — almost never works, find a native equivalent or rephrase.
Excessive exclamation marks and emojis in 'energetic' Arabic copy — feels like 2015 brand voice. Modern native copy is calmer and trusts the reader.
Generic ad copy starters: 'هل تعلم أن...' / 'في عالم اليوم...' / 'نحن نؤمن بأن...' — instant ad-detection signal, scrolled past instantly.

young_urban_cairo: TikTok-native Gen Z slang (فالصو, روش, موود, vibe)
Short sentences, fragmented rhythm, comma-splices intentional
Frequent rhetorical questions ('يا جماعة هو ده طبيعي؟')
Brand voice that 'gets it' — not trying to sound young, just is
alexandria: Some residual Italian/Greek loanwords in older speakers (fading in Gen Z)
Strong regional pride — references to البحر, السيدة, sporting clubs land well
More relaxed, less status-conscious tone than Cairo urban
delta_damanhur_mansoura_tanta: Closer to Cairo than to Saidi — minimal accent distance
Strong sense of regional identity — 'بحري' references resonate
Slightly more conservative tone than Cairo Gen Z but not dramatically
Marker phrases reference local landmarks, family, and seasonal agriculture
upper_egypt_saidi: Distinctive g→g pronunciation (gameel for جميل) — DO NOT phonetically render in copy
Use professional_casual or corporate_formal as default register

example_translations.english: This product is amazing, you have to try it.
example_translations.wrong_msa: هذا المنتج رائع، يجب أن تجربه.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_casual: المنتج ده هايل والله، لازم تجربه.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_genz: المنتج ده vibes صدقني، جربه وهتشكرني.
example_translations.note: Avoid تحفة as the default — overused. Hayel (هايل) feels fresher in 2025-26.

example_translations.english: Limited stock — order now before it's gone.
example_translations.wrong_msa: الكمية محدودة، اطلب الآن قبل النفاد.
example_translations.wrong_translated_feel: ستوك محدود — اطلب الآن قبل أن ينتهي.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_casual: الكمية محدودة، اطلب دلوقتي قبل ما تخلص.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_genz: الكمية بتخلص بسرعة — اطلب دلوقتي قبل ما تندم.
example_translations.note: دلوقتي (now) and خلص (run out) are the natural Egyptian verbs here. 'الآن' sounds like a TV news ticker.

example_translations.english: Honestly, I never thought I'd find something this good for this price.
example_translations.wrong_msa: بصراحة، لم أكن أتوقع أن أجد شيئاً بهذه الجودة بهذا السعر.
example_translations.wrong_translated_feel: بصراحة، ما كنتش متوقع ألاقي حاجة بالجودة دي بالسعر ده.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_casual: بجد ماكنتش متخيل ألاقي حاجة بالجمال ده بالسعر ده.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_genz: بجد، ده انا قلبي وقع — ايه الجودة دي بالسعر ده!
example_translations.note: 'ده انا قلبي وقع' is a recent Gen Z cairo idiom for 'I was floored' — works in late-2024/2025 TikTok content.

example_translations.english: Free delivery across Egypt within 48 hours.
example_translations.wrong_msa: توصيل مجاني إلى جميع أنحاء مصر خلال 48 ساعة.
example_translations.wrong_translated_feel: ديليفيري فري لكل مصر في خلال 48 ساعة.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_casual: شحن مجاني لكل المحافظات، يوصلك في 48 ساعة.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_professional: نوصلك لأي محافظة في مصر خلال 48 ساعة، والشحن علينا.
example_translations.note: 'الشحن علينا' is warmer than 'شحن مجاني' for B2C. Avoid mid-sentence English unless brand voice is heavily code-switching.

example_translations.english: Book a free consultation with our growth team.
example_translations.wrong_msa: احجز استشارة مجانية مع فريق النمو لدينا.
example_translations.wrong_translated_feel: احجز كونسيلتيشن فري مع الـ growth team بتاعنا.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_professional_casual: احجز جلسة استشارية مجانية مع تيم growth عندنا.
example_translations.correct_egyptian_corporate_formal: احجز استشارة مجانية مع فريق النمو لدينا واكتشف فرص توسعك القادمة.
example_translations.note: B2B Egypt LinkedIn lands best with light EN-AR code-switch. Pure MSA reads stiff for SaaS audiences.

fading_terms: حلال عليك (still warm but not Gen Z)
dead_terms: كوول written as كوول (Gen Z just writes 'cool')
